source_text: Ὁμοίως πάλιν περὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ ὁρίζει ἐν ἄλλῳ προφήτῃ λέγοντι: Καὶ πότε ταῦτα συντελεσθήσεται; λέγει κύριος: ὅταν ξύλον κλιθῇ καὶ ἀναστῇ, καὶ ὅταν ἐκ ξύλου αἷμα στάξῃ. ἔχεις πάλιν περὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ τοῦ σταυροῦσθαι μέλλοντος. λέγει δὲ πάλιν τῷ Μωῡσῇ, πολεμουμένου τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων, καὶ ἵνα ὑπομνήσῃ αὐτοὺς πολεμουμένους, ὅτι διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν παρεδόθησαν εἰς θάνατον: λέγει εἰς τὴν καρδίαν Μωϋσέως τὸ πνεῦμα, ἵνα ποιήσῃ τύπον σταυροῦ καὶ τοῦ μέλλοντος πάσχειν, ὅτι, ἐὰν μή, φησίν, ἐλπίσωσιν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα πολεμηθήσονται. τίθησιν οὖν Μωϋσῆς ἓν ἐφ̓ ἓν ὅπλον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς πυγμῆς, καὶ ὑψηλότερος σταθεὶς πάντων ἐξέτεινεν τὰς χεῖρας, καὶ οὕτως πάλιν ἐνίκα ὁ Ἰσραήλ. εἶτα, ὁπόταν καθεῖλεν, ἐθανατοῦντο. πρὸς τί; ἵνα γνῶσιν ὅτι οὐ δύνανται σωθῆναι, ἑὰν μὴ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἐλπίσωσιν. καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἑτέρῳ προφήτῃ λέγει: Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου πρὸς λαὸν ἀπειθῆ καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα ὁδῷ δικαίᾳ μου. πάλιν Μωϋσῆς ποιεῖ τύπον τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν παθεῖν, καὶ αὐτὸς ζωοποιήσει, ὃν δόξουσιν ἀπολωλεκέναι, ἐν σημείῳ πίπτοντος τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ʽἐποίησεν γὰρ κύριος πάντα ὄφιν δάκνειν αὐτούς, καὶ ἀπέθνησκον ἐπειδὴ ἡ παράβασις διὰ τοῦ ὄφεως ἐν Εὔᾳ ἐγένετὀ. ἵνα ἐλέγξῃ αὐτούς. ὅτι διὰ τὴν παράβασιν αὐτῶν εἰς θλῖψιν θανάτου παραδοθήσονται. πέρας γέ τοι αὐτὸς Μωϋσῆς ἐντειλάμενος: Οὐκ ἔσται ὑμῖν οὔτε χωνευτὸν οὔτε γλυπτὸν εἰς θεὸν ὑμῖν. αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, ἵνα τύπον τοῦ Ἰησοῦ δείξῃ. ποιεῖ οὖν Μωϋσῆς χαλκοῦν ὄφιν καὶ τίθησιν ἐνδόξως καὶ κηρύγματι καλεῖ τὸν λαόν. ἐλθόντες οὖν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἐδέοντο Μωῦσέως, ἵνα περὶ αὐτῶν ἀνενέγκῃ δέησιν περὶ τῆς ἰάσεως αὐτῶν. εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς Μωϋσῆς: Ὅταν, φησίν. δηχθῇ τις ὑμῶν, ἐλθέτω ἐπὶ τὸν ὄφιν τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ ξύλου ἐπικείμενον καὶ ἐλπισάτω πιστεύσας, ὅτι αὐτὸς ὢν νεκρὸς δύναται ζωοποιῆσαι, καὶ παραχρῆμα σωθήσεται. καὶ οὕτως ἐποίουν. ἔχεις πάλιν καὶ ἐν τούτοις τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ πάντα καὶ εἰς αὐτόν. τί λέγει πάλιν Μωϋσῆς Ἰησοῦ, υἱῷ Ναυή, ἐπιθεὶς αὐτῷ τοῦτο τὸ ὄνομα, ὄντι προφήτῃ, ἵνα μόνον ἀκούσῃ πᾶς ὁ λαός; ὅτι πάντα ὁ πατὴρ φανεροῖ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ Ἰησοῦ. λέγει οὖν Μωϋσῆς Ἰησοῦ, υἱῷ Ναυή, ἐπιθεὶς τοῦτο τὸ ὄνομα, ὁπότε ἔπεμψεν αὐτὸν κατάσκοπον τῆς γῆς: Λάβε βιβλίον εἰς τὰς χεῖράς σου καὶ γράψον, ἃ λέγει κύριος, ὅτι ἐκκόψει ἐκ ῥιζῶν τὸν οἶκον πάντα τοῦ Ἀμαλὴκ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπ’ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν. ἴδε πάλιν Ἰησοῦς, οὐχὶ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου, ἀλλὰ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, τύπῳ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ φανερωθείς. ἐπεὶ οὖν μέλλουσιν λέγειν, ὅτι Χριστὸς υἱὸς Δαυείδ ἐστιν, αὐτὸς προφητεύει Δαυείδ, φοβούμενος καὶ συνίων τὴν πλάνην τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν: Εἷπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου: Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου, ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου. καὶ πάλιν λέγει οὕτως Ἡσαΐας: Εἷπεν κύριος τῷ Χριστῷ μου κυρίῳ. οὗ ἐκράτησα τῆς δεξιᾶς αὐτοῦ, ἐπακοῦσαι ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ἔθνη, καὶ ἰσχὺν βασιλέων διαρρήξω. ἴδε, πῶς Δαυεὶδ λέγει αὐτὸν κύριον. καὶ υἱὸν οὐ λέγει.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly again concerning the cross He defines in another prophet saying: And when will these things be fulfilled? says the Lord: when wood is bent and rises, and when from wood blood drips. You have again concerning the cross and the one about to be crucified. And He says again to Moses, when Israel was being warred against by the aliens, and so that He might remind them, being warred against, that on account of their sins they were handed over to death: He says into the heart of Moses the Spirit, so that He might make a type of cross and of the one about to suffer, because, if not, He says, they will hope in Him, they will be warred against forever. Therefore Moses puts one upon one weapon in the middle of the fist, and having stood higher than all, he extended his hands, and thus again Israel was victorious. Then, as often as he let down, they were being killed. Why? So that they might know that they are not able to be saved if they do not hope in Him. And again in another prophet He says: The whole day I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contradicting people on the way of my righteousness. Again Moses makes a type of Jesus, because He must suffer, and He will make alive the one they think to have lost, in the sign of the falling of Israel, for the Lord made all a serpent to bite them, and they were dying because the transgression through the serpent happened in Eve. So that He might convict them, because on account of their transgression they will be handed over to death's affliction. For Moses, having been commanded, says: There will not be for you either a molten or a carved thing into a god for you. He Himself does, so that He might show a type of Jesus. Therefore Moses makes a bronze serpent and puts it in a glorious and proclaimed way and calls the people. Having come therefore to the same place, they were begging Moses, so that he might carry up a prayer concerning their healing. And Moses said to them: When anyone of you is bitten, let him come to the serpent on the wood suspended and let him hope, having believed, that He, being dead, is able to make alive, and immediately he will be saved. And thus they were doing. You have again, also in these things, the glory of Jesus, because in Him are all things and to Him. What does Moses say again to Jesus, son of Nun, having imposed this name on him, being a prophet, so that only all the people might hear? Because all things the Father makes clear concerning the Son Jesus. Therefore Moses says to Jesus, son of Nun, having imposed this name on him, when he sent him as a spy of the land: Take a book into your hands and write what the Lord says, because He will cut off from the roots the whole house of Amalek, the Son of God, in the last of the days. See again Jesus, not a son of man, but a Son of God, having been revealed in flesh in type. Since therefore they are about to say that Christ is a son of David, He Himself prophesies through David, fearing and understanding the error of the sinners: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies as a footstool under your feet. And again Isaiah says thus: The Lord said to my Christ, my Lord. Whom I held by the right hand, to hear before Him the nations, and I will tear the strength of kings. See, how David calls Him Lord. And he does not call Him son.

pass_b_english: Once more the author defines the cross through another prophet who asks, 'When will these things be fulfilled?' The Lord answers: 'When wood is bent and rises again, and when blood drips from wood.' Here again we find a reference to the cross and to the one who was about to be crucified.

The text then turns to Moses. While Israel was being attacked by foreign nations, the Spirit spoke into Moses' heart to remind the embattled people that their sins had handed them over to death. The Spirit instructed Moses to fashion a type of the cross and of the one who would suffer, declaring, 'If they do not put their hope in him, they will be warred against forever.' So Moses placed one weapon upon another in the midst of the battle, stood higher than everyone else, and stretched out his hands. When he did this, Israel prevailed; whenever he lowered his hands, they were cut down. This happened so they would understand that they cannot be saved unless they hope in him.
Another prophet echoes the same truth: 'All day long I have stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people who walk in a way that is not right.'

Moses again provides a type of Jesus. Because Jesus must suffer, he will give life to the one they suppose to be lost. This sign appears in the defeat of Israel: the Lord sent serpents to bite them, and they died because the transgression that began through the serpent in Eve had come to full fruit. The purpose was to convict them, since their transgression would hand them over to death's affliction.

Moses himself had been commanded, 'You shall not have any molten or carved image as a god.' Yet he himself acts in order to display a type of Jesus. He makes a bronze serpent, sets it up gloriously with a proclamation, and summons the people. When they gather, they beg Moses to intercede for their healing. He tells them: 'Whenever any of you is bitten, let him come to the serpent suspended on the wood, look to it in faith, believing that the one who is dead can make alive, and he will be saved at once.' And they did exactly that.
In these events, too, you see the glory of Jesus: all things are in him and for him.

What does Moses say to Jesus the son of Nun after giving him that name — a prophet — so that all the people might hear? He does it because the Father reveals everything concerning the Son Jesus. When Moses sends him as a spy into the land, he commands, 'Take a book in your hands and write what the Lord says: the Son of God will cut off the entire house of Amalek from its roots at the end of the days.' See here again Jesus — not a son of man, but the Son of God, revealed in flesh as a type.

Since some were about to claim that the Christ is merely a son of David, David himself prophesies, fearing and discerning the error of sinners: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet"' (Psalm 110:1). And Isaiah declares likewise: 'The Lord said to my Christ, my Lord, whose right hand I have grasped, to make nations listen before him, and I will shatter the strength of kings' (Isaiah 45:1). Notice: David calls him Lord, not son.

review.notes: Pass B fails on completeness and accuracy regarding the phrase 'ἐν μέσῳ τῆς πυγμῆς'. The Greek 'πυγμῆς' (fist) is translated in Pass B as 'in the midst of the battle', which is a significant semantic shift/interpretation not present in the Greek or Pass A. Pass A correctly translates it as 'in the middle of the fist'. Additionally, Pass B omits the specific detail 'ἐν Εὔᾳ ἐγένετο' (happened in Eve) by paraphrasing it as 'began through the serpent in Eve', though this is a minor interpretive difference compared to the 'fist/battle' error.
reasons: Pass B translates 'ἐν μέσῳ τῆς πυγμῆς' (in the middle of the fist) as 'in the midst of the battle', which is an interpretive addition/substitution not found in the source text or Pass A.
